Every link below was loaded with `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200) and its page title checked, unless
noted. Official sources come first.

## Curated links

- **[NOT-OD-24-157: Implementation Update for Data Management and Access Practices Under the Genomic Data Sharing Policy](https://grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/notice-files/NOT-OD-24-157.html)**
  (NIH Guide) — the notice the questionnaire's "NIST SP 800-171" line most plausibly traces to. Use it
  to read the Scope and Applicability section and the "Security Best Practices for Users of
  Controlled-Access Data" section yourself. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200; title
  matches).

- **[Genomic Data Sharing Policy](https://sharing.nih.gov/genomic-data-sharing-policy)** (NIH,
  sharing.nih.gov) — NIH's hub page for the GDS Policy and controlled-access data. Use it when someone
  proposes requesting genomic data and you need the process and the current security documents. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200; title "Genomic Data Sharing Policy | Grants & Funding").

- **[45 CFR 164.312, Technical safeguards](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.312)** (Cornell
  LII) — access control, audit controls, integrity, authentication, transmission security. The
  technical core of the EXT-21 control set. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[45 CFR 164.308, Administrative safeguards](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.308)**
  (Cornell LII) — risk analysis, activity review, termination procedures, incident response, backup.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[45 CFR 164.402, Definitions (breach)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.402)** (Cornell
  LII) — the breach definition, the presumption and the four-factor assessment. Use it for the
  misdirected-file conversation with the privacy officer. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13
  (HTTP 200).

- **[45 CFR 164.514, Other requirements relating to uses and disclosures of PHI](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514)**
  (Cornell LII) — paragraph (e) is the limited data set and the DUA terms, including the recipient's
  duty to report misuse. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[42 U.S.C. 241, Research and investigations generally](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/241)**
  (Cornell LII) — subsection (d) is the Certificate of Confidentiality statute, including "all copies"
  and "for perpetuity." Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2, Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/171/r2/upd1/final)**
  (NIST CSRC) — the standard the notice names. Read it from NIST before anyone commits Lakeshore to it
  for anything. This lesson doesn't state its requirements, and which revision NIH expects is something
  to confirm in NIH's own documents. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5, Recommendation for Key Management: General](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/57/pt1/r5/final)**
  (NIST CSRC) — the reference vocabulary for key lifecycle: generation, storage, rotation, revocation,
  destruction. Use it when writing the key-handling control. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13
  (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST IR 7966, Security of Interactive and Automated Access Management Using Secure Shell (SSH)](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ir/7966/final)**
  (NIST CSRC) — practical guidance on managing SSH keys for automated transfers, which is the kind of
  credential an sFTP job uses. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

**No video embed for this module.** Searched for a video on NIH's controlled-access genomic data
security notice and on NIST SP 800-171; the only candidates were on non-YouTube hosts (an NIH VideoCast
page, a Defense Department site) or vendor webinars. The two government videos relevant to the HIPAA
side (HHS's Security Rule cybersecurity video and OCR's risk management video) verified through
YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-13 but are already embedded elsewhere in the curriculum, in
[investigating a healthcare data incident](../../healthcare-security-and-privacy/investigating-a-healthcare-data-incident/index.qmd)
and [information governance in a covered entity](../../healthcare-security-and-privacy/information-governance-in-a-covered-entity/index.qmd).

Not listed: NIH's "Security Best Practices for Users of Controlled-Access Data" document (the notice
names it, but the PDF address I tried returned a generic NIH page title to `curl`, so I could not
confirm its content), NIH's Certificates of Confidentiality page (the connection failed with a proxy
error and was not retried) and HHS's breach and encryption guidance pages (HTTP 403, not retried).

## Keep learning

Not official sources, and not authority for any regulatory claim.

- **[Key Management Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Key_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html)**
  (OWASP) — practitioner-written, concrete advice on key generation, storage, rotation and separation.
  Good for turning the key-handling control into a checklist. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-13 (HTTP 200; title "Key Management - OWASP Cheat Sheet Series").

- **[Logging Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html)**
  (OWASP) — what to log, what not to log (including sensitive data), and how to protect logs. Useful
  for the "keep donor data out of the logs" rule. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200;
  title "Logging - OWASP Cheat Sheet Series").

- **[SP 800-92, Guide to Computer Security Log Management](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/92/final)**
  (NIST CSRC) — older but still a clear walkthrough of log generation, storage and review. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[SP 800-61 Rev. 2, Computer Security Incident Handling Guide](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r2/final)**
  (NIST CSRC) — the standard incident-handling lifecycle; a good base for the EXT-21 incident plan's IT
  portion. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[HIPAA Encryption Requirements](https://www.hipaajournal.com/hipaa-encryption-requirements/)**
  (HIPAA Journal; commercial publisher, also sells training) — a readable explainer of how
  "addressable" encryption is treated in practice. Treat as commentary and check any claim against the
  rule text. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200; title "HIPAA Encryption Requirements
  - 2026 Update").
